nodes.label: Who raises it  ·  seven
nodes.sub: A doctor in an ED may only raise it as an ED referral — they cannot claim another source.

nodes.label: A referral is raised
nodes.sub: Somebody has decided this person needs to go somewhere.

nodes.label: Addressed to up to three places at once
nodes.sub: Up to the configured recipient cap. Distinct named psychiatric wards can be addressed together; duplicate recipients and mixing a broad ward request with named ward requests are refused.

nodes.label: ①  Sent to a community team
nodes.sub: Named as free text — there is no register of teams to choose from.
nodes.patient: At home, or wherever they were.
nodes.bed: Nothing. This arm never involves one.

nodes.label: ②  Sent to a psychiatric ward
nodes.sub: Carries what the bed must be: sex, gender, secure, involuntary, high-acuity nursing.

nodes.label: ③  Sent to an emergency department
nodes.sub: Must say what it is FOR: a bed, a psychiatric review, or a medical assessment.
nodes.patient: On their way to, or already in, that department.

nodes.label: Accepted — community follow-up
nodes.sub: The arm ends here. It never becomes a bed search.

nodes.label: Declined — four reasons
nodes.sub: Outside the team's catchment · needs inpatient care, not community follow-up · the client declined or could not be contacted · already open to another team.

nodes.label: No answer yet
nodes.sub: The arm remains queued until answered or withdrawn. Other acceptances do not cancel a community arm. Displayed waiting/overdue indicators do not decide or close it.
nodes.finding: Nothing anywhere can close a queued community arm except the team answering or the referrer.

nodes.label: The referrer withdraws just this arm
nodes.sub: A narrow exception added 17 September 2026, and only while the arm is still queued — a team that has already answered keeps its answer. The bed request stands.

nodes.label: It can also begin part-way through a bed search
nodes.sub: Redirecting a bed search to a community team raises a real referral of this kind — or reuses a queued arm already asking that same team, rather than asking twice. So this arm does not only start at the front door.

nodes.label: This arm is exempt from the automatic cancellation
nodes.sub: In both directions. A ward accepting does not close it, and it accepting does not close the bed search. It is the only arm that behaves this way.

nodes.label: Accepted
nodes.sub: Records the ward answer, with an optional named bed reservation on the referral. It creates no movement or admission.
nodes.bed: No movement pull yet; a named bed can be reserved on this answer.

nodes.label: Declined — seven reasons
nodes.sub: No suitable bed · age band not provided here · no bed of that designation · no secure bed · belongs to another service · referred elsewhere · another reason.

nodes.label: No answer at all
nodes.sub: The destination remains waiting until answered, withdrawn or cancelled by a competing acceptance. Current target/overdue displays can flag waiting; they do not choose an answer.

nodes.label: Every other waiting arm is cancelled
nodes.sub: Automatically, the moment a ward OR a department accepts — except the community arm, which is exempt in both directions. The referrer is neither asked nor told.

nodes.label: The referrer takes the WHOLE referral back
nodes.sub: The default, and the opposite of the community arm's one-arm exception: every still-queued destination goes at once. If a bed search is already running it releases the held bed and cancels the transport, and closes as 'did not proceed'. Refused once transport has collected the patient — that needs a coordinator, not an automatic withdrawal.

nodes.label: A ward cannot accept while a department's bed search is live
nodes.sub: One referral, two arms: if the emergency department already raised the bed search, the ward arm is refused until that movement closes or arrives. Neither arm's screen shows the other.

nodes.label: It lands on that department's board
nodes.sub: And the referrer can see their patient sitting there.

nodes.label: Expected to arrive
nodes.sub: Triaged, and not here yet. It sits on a separate list from the referrals.

nodes.label: Expected, and never arrives
nodes.sub: A queued ED arm can be declined or withdrawn before arrival, removing this expectation. Otherwise it stays until arrival; past 72 hours the screen adds a reminder but changes no record.
nodes.finding: A queued ED arm can be declined or withdrawn before arrival; the expectation then disappears without an arrival stamp.

nodes.label: Marked present
nodes.sub: The only door between the two lists. Stamped once; a repeat keeps the earliest time.

nodes.label: Accepted — the department takes them
nodes.sub: And every other destination still waiting is cancelled on the spot, including the ward request sent alongside it. The referrer is not asked.

nodes.label: Declined — three reasons only
nodes.sub: Belongs to another service · referred elsewhere · another reason. The four bed-shaped reasons are withheld on purpose: an ED is not being asked for a bed.

nodes.label: A doctor raises a bed search from here
nodes.sub: This is what creates the record that moves. It can be linked back to the referral that sent them, or raised for somebody nobody referred.

nodes.label: The department decides no bed is needed
nodes.sub: Two labels, one behaviour: 'for community follow-up' raises no referral and tells no team — only the separate action below does that. Unwinds a held bed, an uncollected transport job and every live ward request. Refused once transport has collected them.

nodes.label: Referred straight to a community team instead
nodes.sub: Ends the bed search and creates or reuses a real community referral. Available from the moment the bed search exists until the patient is collected — not only from a department. Refused once they are collected, and while a legal form has no conclusive examination outcome.

nodes.label: Left the department
nodes.sub: Only recordable after an outcome has been recorded first.

nodes.label: A separate movement is raised
nodes.sub: Acceptance does not create the bed-search record. RAISE_REFERRAL creates it separately and can link it to the referral.

nodes.label: Wards are asked
nodes.sub: One at a time, or several at once, up to three.

nodes.label: A ward accepts in principle
nodes.sub: Still no bed set aside.

nodes.label: A bed is pulled and held
nodes.sub: Empty, offered to nobody else. Four hours is the default, not a rule — a coordinator can set the hold anywhere between thirty minutes and four hours. The admission this creates now names the movement it came from — a join added by owner ruling on 21 September, and the first pointer of any kind between the patient's track and the bed's; it is empty for the beds seeded as already occupied, so anything reading it has to cope with nothing being there.

nodes.label: Transport is booked
nodes.sub: Five answers, none defaulted — provider, escort, CAD number, voluntary or involuntary, estimated time.

nodes.label: The crew accepts, and sets off
The patient is collected
nodes.sub: After this point, everything changes.
nodes.patient: In a vehicle, between two places.

nodes.label: The ward says they have arrived
nodes.sub: Ward confirmation closes the movement and records the occupied stay. An officer Delivered stamp ends only the transport leg. STEP_BACK_STAGE refuses arrival; a separate scoped, time-limited Undo can correct the latest unchanged arrival snapshot.

nodes.label: Clinically ready to leave
nodes.sub: The patient's departure and the named bed-release record proceed on two tracks.
nodes.patient: Finished with hospital, possibly still in the bed.

nodes.label: A ward declines — seven reasons
nodes.sub: No bed · sex mix · no specialling · acuity mix · capability mismatch · bed pulled for an earlier referral · out of catchment.

nodes.label: One ward's request is taken back
nodes.sub: Seven reasons. The other wards asked carry on considering.

nodes.label: The acceptance is withdrawn
nodes.sub: A listed reason records why the acceptance is withdrawn. An uncollected pulled or stepped-back hold is released in the same act; cancel a live job first. Handover-ready and moving are refused.

nodes.label: The bed search is abandoned
nodes.sub: Pulled from every ward still considering it, or — once a ward has accepted — the acceptance revoked and any held bed given back. It closes as 'did not proceed'. This is also where an examination outcome of a community order, or a revocation, lands while no bed is held yet.

nodes.label: The held bed is given back — four reasons
nodes.sub: NINE different actions delete that admission, not one — releasing the pull (four reasons of its own), releasing a held bed after transport was stopped, abandoning the bed search, the referrer withdrawing it, the department deciding no bed is needed, sending them to a community team instead, an examination outcome that ends it, releasing the bed a diverted journey held, and releasing the bed while reopening the search. Whichever it was, the admission record is deleted outright: nobody was ever in this bed.

nodes.label: Transport cancelled before collection
nodes.sub: A listed reason removes the job without moving the stage or automatically rebooking. The held-bed notice checks the admission link as well as stage, including a stepped-back pull.
nodes.finding: The role/booking-place, collected, delivered and closed checks are distinct; an officer delivery can precede ward arrival without closure.

nodes.label: The journey is stopped after collection
nodes.sub: Three reasons, and somebody must say where the patient now is. The movement closes and the bed stays held.
nodes.finding: An officer delivery can precede ward arrival without closure, so delivered and closed refusal paths are distinct.

nodes.label: Absent without leave is recorded
nodes.sub: The occupied stay and held bed remain. The ward records absence, its steps and return against the admission; the current order can also create an action-inbox fact.

nodes.label: A coordinator places them anyway
nodes.sub: Eight of the bed checks can be passed by recording one of five reasons — the receiving team has agreed despite the mismatch · clinical urgency outweighs it · the bed information is known to be out of date · continuity with an earlier admission here · closer to home or family. Running out of one-to-one nursing or of high-acuity capacity can be passed the same way, and passing the acuity one also demands that the nurse unit manager was consulted.

nodes.label: The one refusal nothing can override
nodes.sub: If the ward is designated for one gender and the patient's recorded gender is the other, no reason passes it and the app will not even offer the list. Non-binary, Different term, and not-recorded genders can use the coordinator-reviewed exception. Every other bed check here can be forced; this one cannot.

nodes.label: A patient with a non-binary, Different term, or unrecorded gender onto a single-gender ward
nodes.sub: Only a coordinator, and only with one of six recorded reasons — a single room is available · the patient's stated preference, agreed with the ward · no single room is free and the ward agreed a plan for privacy · the only suitable ready bed, agreed with the ward · they know this ward from an earlier stay · closer to home or supports.

nodes.label: Record a form from the Forms page
nodes.sub: The form selector and checked paper time reach the supported form-writing handler. Authorised users can save; refusal keeps the draft and shows the reason. This does not issue a legal instrument or calculate its statutory expiry.

nodes.label: No transport needed
nodes.sub: Marked arrived straight from the held bed, with no journey recorded at all.

nodes.label: Pulling again when the bed is already held
nodes.sub: Restoring an already-linked hold preserves its bed rather than consuming another. Current code rechecks the matching admission, patient placement, observation/high-acuity staffing, legal authority and gender before restoring the pulled stage.
nodes.finding: Restoring a hold does not consume a second bed; staffing, legal, gender and matching-admission checks still run.

nodes.label: A held destination no longer suits
nodes.sub: Current gender/legal facts are checked at forward steps. WITHDRAW_ACCEPTANCE can release an uncollected pulled or stepped-back hold atomically after any live job is cancelled; no obsolete three-step sequence should be assumed.
nodes.finding: A held acceptance can now be withdrawn atomically after cancelling a live job; handover-ready/moving still require the supported earlier-stage path.

nodes.label: Cancellation keeps the bed facts separate
nodes.sub: The hold is detected from the linked admission OR the pulled-or-later stage. Cancelling removes the job and preserves the bed and current stage, including after a step back.
nodes.finding: Cancellation checks both the admission link and stage before describing whether the bed stays held.

nodes.label: The legal authority is revoked before collection
nodes.sub: A revoked examination while a bed is held records the examination and flags release without refunding the bed. Acceptance, en-route and collection refuse while that hold is unresolved; physical arrival remains recordable.

nodes.label: Away at an ED, or on leave
nodes.sub: An ED trip and leave name the occupied admission. Return records clear the relevant absence. Leave also records its kind and optional psychiatrist-authorisation answer; the bed stays held while away.

nodes.label: Closure limits corrections; admitted forms have a separate route
nodes.sub: Most movement actions refuse closure. The admitting ward can still record a supported written form or typed expiry for a current occupied stay. STEP_BACK_STAGE refuses arrival, while a separate scoped Undo can reverse the latest unchanged transport/arrival snapshot within its window.
nodes.finding: Most movement commands refuse closure, but admitted-ward form and expiry commands have explicit supported post-arrival routes.

nodes.label: Sending a country patient home
nodes.sub: Logged against the admission once it has been arranged off the system: home hospital, whether its ward agreed, road or flight, provider and tracking number. It books nothing. Only when the home ward agreed does it also open a new movement asking for a bed at home.

nodes.label: Track one — the person leaves
nodes.sub: Eight recorded departure destinations. A psychiatric transfer releases the sending ward bed while taking a receiving bed.
nodes.bed: Normally empty and allocatable rise once and the live release completes; an over-capacity arrival conflict is reconciled without inventing an extra bed.

nodes.label: Track two — the bed is released
nodes.sub: Expected can go directly to discharged or pass through confirmed. The named admission leaving completes its release in the same write; capacity reconciliation prevents counting an already-recorded release or an over-capacity arrival twice.
nodes.patient: Names the stay it belongs to, and nothing else about them.
nodes.bed: Counted as available again, at the last step only.

nodes.label: Stuck, or waiting on something
nodes.sub: Seven things it can wait on, nine reasons it can be stuck. Neither is a stage.

nodes.label: Discharged to the community
nodes.sub: Frees a bed.

nodes.label: Transferred to another psychiatric ward
nodes.sub: Frees THIS ward's bed and gains the state nothing — the only one that is not a release.

nodes.label: Transferred to a general hospital
nodes.sub: Frees a bed.

nodes.label: Moved to residential care
nodes.sub: Frees a bed.

nodes.label: Left against advice
nodes.sub: Frees a bed.

nodes.label: Died on the ward
nodes.sub: Frees a bed.

nodes.label: Transferred to police or prison custody
nodes.sub: Frees a bed.

nodes.label: Did not return
nodes.sub: Frees a bed.

nodes.label: Is this the same person already?
nodes.sub: Duplicate matching warns about number and demographic similarities. A duplicate record number blocks registration in both form and reducer; name similarity alone remains a review warning.

nodes.label: Add patient saves identity; referral saves intake
nodes.sub: The current Add patient form asks for identity, optional gender and Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander status. Clinical intake and location belong to the referral flow. Obsolete non-working Print/Save draft controls are hidden; the historical silent-discard finding no longer describes this screen.

nodes.label: Is the patient medically cleared?
nodes.sub: Three answers, not two — unrecorded, cleared, and explicitly not cleared.

nodes.label: The display follows wall-clock time
nodes.sub: The provider updates elapsed wall-clock time at minute boundaries and catches up when the page becomes visible. A controlled test clock is separate. A display becoming overdue does not by itself prove that a domain action ran; check the event handler for that action.

nodes.label: Settings change current operational defaults
nodes.sub: WardConfiguration carries twelve fields: access/decision/transfer/booking targets, parallel-recipient cap, pull hold, morning deadline, due-soon warnings and Forecast thresholds. A valid full draft is merged against its baseline or refused for conflicting fields; old optional keys take documented defaults.

nodes.label: Where they sit in the queue
nodes.sub: Flagged urgent first, then the urgency tier, then whoever has waited longest, then the record's own id as a tie-break. Nothing else moves anybody up.

nodes.label: Duplicate bed requests are surfaced
nodes.sub: The current duplicate-bed-request derivation finds multiple active requests for one linked patient and creates a coordinator fact row. It does not rank patients or choose a winner. This is distinct from a physical double-booking check.

nodes.label: Flagged urgent
nodes.sub: Ten reasons. Lifts the patient above every urgency level, and re-sorts nothing on its own.

nodes.label: Escalated
nodes.sub: Which wards were tried and who was rung. Six people it can be escalated to.

nodes.label: A ward states how many beds it can allocate
nodes.sub: Set outright rather than counted up, and refused if it claims more beds than the ward physically has. Asking a ward to refresh it records that somebody asked, and moves no number at all.

nodes.label: The legal status changes
nodes.sub: Four values. Changing it triggers nothing — even if it makes the accepted ward unlawful.

nodes.label: The legal paperwork arrives
nodes.sub: Nine forms can be recorded as received — 1A, 3A, 3C, 3D, 5A, 5B, 6A, 6B, 6C. Receipt can be undone and recorded again; every expiry is a time a clinician typed.

nodes.label: An examination is recorded
nodes.sub: Four outcomes. Only “a further examination is ordered” allows a second one.

nodes.label: The paperwork is written, continued, or attached
nodes.sub: Written and continued forms record paper facts and clear legacy calculated clocks; same-form written-time edits preserve applicable typed facts. An admitted ward has a post-arrival route. A3C after3D is refused. A country1A extension requires a current country setting and a finite typed later paper expiry; no statutory duration is computed.

nodes.label: The ward's authority does not match the person's status
nodes.sub: Two shapes, both named: an involuntary patient on a voluntary ward, and a voluntary patient on a locked one. It can be flagged, and it cannot be overridden: ward authority for an involuntary patient is never overridable (owner ruling, 25 September).

nodes.label: Somebody is told
nodes.sub: Twenty-four kinds of notice. Written once, never rewritten, never deleted, never expiring.

nodes.label: The journey is diverted while it is under way
nodes.sub: Only once the patient is actually in the vehicle — it is refused before collection, after arrival, and a second time on a movement already diverted. It records a reason and where they were taken instead. The held bed does not come back on its own: giving it back is a separate act, and refused unless this movement was in fact diverted.

nodes.label: Expiry can be recorded for an admitted patient
nodes.sub: The legal-event handler permits the ward to record a typed expiry for its admitted patient even when the movement is closed. This is a recorded time, not a computed legal limit. See ward-flow-record-legal-events.ts.
nodes.finding: The admitted-patient expiry route is implemented for the ward. Read the current legal-event handler; the old closed-movement gap is retired.

nodes.label: A clock somebody starts by hand
nodes.sub: Two kinds, forty-eight hours and seven days, raised against a movement and cleared again. Only one can be open at a time — raising a second is refused, and so is clearing one that was never raised. Nothing starts it automatically and nothing expires it; it is a note about time, not a timer.

nodes.label: The rule for a bed kept during a medical trip
nodes.sub: The unwired retention helper keeps the bed by default, including above the24-hour threshold; above threshold adds requiresReview. Only an explicit override changes freesBed. The numeric constant is24 while an adjacent historical provenance comment still says48.

nodes.label: A row appears in the coordinator's inbox
nodes.sub: The current inbox derives fact rows from movements, stays, planned bookings and bed-meeting actions. Facts are acknowledged/owned/snoozed, never ticked away. The daily check is a commitment; its day-shaped ID can be completed and reopened.
nodes.finding: Completion applies to commitment IDs; fact rows use their source condition and bed-meeting actions have a dedicated completion event.

nodes.label: Step-down, and what is holding the discharge up
nodes.sub: Two settings on a known admission: step-down candidacy and one discharge barrier. The acting ward must match; a substantive barrier is refused for a stay under seven days. Neither moves a bed figure.

nodes.label: A discharge recorded the other way
nodes.sub: A second event does exactly what recording a departure does, but only for a patient whose identity is linked, and only against the revision number the screen last read. Same result, different door.

nodes.label: The bed is being prepared
nodes.sub: Cleaning/repair is a separate preparation flag. It does not directly rewrite the ward count, and a bed still being made ready may still be pulled (D-181 item 5).

nodes.label: Only the ward it belongs to may touch it
nodes.sub: Confirming a release, reversing it, flagging it stuck, clearing that flag, marking the bed being cleaned, and finally freeing it are each refused to any other ward. It is what stops one ward's freed bed landing in another ward's figures.

nodes.label: The ward's own day, beside the patient's
nodes.sub: A morning count a ward confirms, a message it can be sent, and a sweep that works out which beds on leave are worth warning about. None of them belongs to any one patient, which is why they sit off the journey rather than on it.

nodes.label: Recorded alongside  ·
nodes.sub: Happens at some point without moving the journey.

nodes.label: ←  Stalls, undos and endings
nodes.sub: Grey goes back into the route. Teal does not.

nodes.label: Read down the middle  ↓
nodes.sub: Read straight down.

nodes.label: Diversions  →
nodes.sub: It carries on, somewhere other than expected.
